title: Her brother George's fall and death in Chicago
summary: She tells how George broke his spine in a fall during a house fire and died in the hospital.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: No, it ain't that old. I said that's when my husband died. _______ wrote that song until -- when the Okay people (unintelligible) and they told me, said, "Sippie, _______ have a song of your own," said, "That's where you make your money _______." "Shorty George" is my first song that I made _______ and then I had to make songs after that (unintelligible) "Bedroom Blues" and I thought about my husband being dead, nobody to love me _______, everybody dead and after Buddy _______ he got off from work and he was running after a streetcar -- he should have got in the cab. But he didn't get a cab, he running after the streetcar, he fell and if the conductor hadn't sent him to the hospital, he might have been a dead man, _______.

My brother, yeah. And the man didn't send my brother to no hospital. They just carried him on and (unintelligible). My brother had done something to his spine, broke his spine. Brought him home and then the house caught fire when he lived there and by that -- Buddy didn't know his

back was broken, see? Buddy got up to go out of the house and he had to go up some kind of steps and it was a platform, you know, going ________ and Buddy was a tall man, you know. And that big ________ down there is just like him. When Buddy fell, the top of his head hit the top of the stairway and knocked him back and by having that back trouble, it killed him. So (unintelligible) told me ________ he was living with some strange people, but by me writing Buddy a letter, and Buddy was ________ with this man, this man didn't know. He say, "Maybe I can find George's sister, Sippie Wallace," (unintelligible) "because he got a letter from her about a couple days ago. Maybe I can find her letter. Her address might be on the letter." Sure enough, it was. They got this letter and my address was on there and so he wrote me a letter and say, "I think you would want to know that your brother George fell and broke his spine and in getting out of the house, the house was on fire, he fell," and he say, "he's dead in the hospital -- in the morgue."

Lord, I had to put him away and me nothing but a girl, you know. I say that liked to have killed me. That liked to have, with my Mama dead, now my brother's done died. I couldn't find nobody -- my sister was dead, too, my older sister. So my cousin went with me and so she came to Chicago with me. I was in Detroit. So she came to Detroit with me to help me along, because I couldn't have made it by myself, because I couldn't have made it. And she helped me. ________
